newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 opens higher as rate worries subside.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 opens higher as rate worries subside.

text.p: UK shares opened higher on Wednesday as investors shook off lingering fears of an interest rate rise ahead of the UK's monthly monetary policy meeting.
Dealers said a technical shortage of stock was also helping to squeeze share prices higher.
"It's no longer about fundamentals, it is all about liquidity and the squeeze, given that the market is technically short of stock we're going to see it squeezed up further yet," one said.
The FTSE index of 100 leading stocks was up 13.4 points at 4,181.6 by 0843 GMT, with gainers outweighing losers by two-to-one.
